learningObjective: Determine loop-invariance of an expression when its operands are themselves defined inside the loop via phi.

canonicalClaims.claim: An expression is loop-invariant iff every operand is either a constant or itself loop-invariant (defined outside the loop or by another loop-invariant expression). Loop-header phi nodes with values that change across iterations make the phi's result loop-variant.
conditions: SSA form with well-defined loop structure (header, body, preheader).
Loop-carried state is expressed via phi nodes.
nonImplications: Does not imply LICM cannot see through phi nodes; the invariance test operates on operand chains.
Does not imply that a loop-variant expression cannot be optimized; strength reduction and IV simplification may apply.

misconceptions.claim: An expression with at least one constant operand is loop-invariant.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Loop-invariance is a conjunction over operands; a single loop-variant operand suffices to make the expression loop-variant.

misconceptions.claim: LICM cannot process loops containing phi nodes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: LICM routinely processes SSA loops with phi at headers; the invariance test explicitly handles phi operands via the invariance chain.

misconceptions.claim: Purity of the operator implies loop-invariance of the expression.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Purity is necessary for safe hoisting, but invariance also requires operand-side invariance.

implementationFacts: LLVM's LICM checks operand-by-operand invariance recursively.
Loop-header phi results are invariant only if both incoming values are invariant (equivalent to a value defined outside the loop).
performanceScenarios: IV strength reduction extracts loop-variant patterns like i*constant into loop-carried recurrences, complementing LICM.
